title: Rotation sensitivity and noise stability
statement: Let $n\ge 0$, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, and let $\theta\in[0,\pi]$. If $\gamma_n$ is standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$ and $\mathbf 1_A$ is the indicator of $A$, then the probability that a standard Gaussian vector and its rotation by angle $\theta$ with an independent standard Gaussian vector disagree on membership in $A$ equals $2\bigl(\gamma_n(A)-\operatorname{Stab}_{\cos\theta}(\mathbf 1_A)\bigr)$, where $\operatorname{Stab}_{\rho}(f)=\mathbb E[f(X)f(\rho X+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}Y)]$ for independent $X,Y\sim\gamma_n$.
